text: Dear customer, this call is from your bank's KYC department. Your KYC documents have expired and your account will be temporarily blocked from this evening.
tell: Banks notify KYC renewal in writing and through the branch or app, with weeks of notice, not same-day blocking calls.

text: Hello sir, I am calling from your mobile network about your SIM card KYC. Your documents were not updated after the new rule, so the SIM will be deactivated within twenty-four hours.
tell: SIM re-verification happens at a store with the original ID, not by phone under a disconnection countdown.

text: Madam, the KYC on your wallet app is still pending, and under the latest RBI guideline unverified wallets are being suspended. I will update it with you on the call itself, it takes two minutes.
tell: Offering to complete verification for you over a call is the setup for collecting codes or installing an app.

text: I am an authorised executive from the head office KYC team, my employee code is K Y C four five eight two. You can check that this phone number is registered with the bank.
tell: Caller ID and recited employee codes are trivially spoofed; verification means calling the number on your card.

text: This is a mandatory Reserve Bank of India directive. Every account holder must re-verify their PAN and Aadhaar linking today, otherwise the account is treated as a benami account.
tell: Invoking the RBI and legal terms like benami to make routine paperwork sound criminal.

text: I can see your details on my screen, your full name, your home branch and the last four digits of your debit card. I am calling from the official verification desk, so there is nothing to worry about.
tell: Reciting leaked partial data to prove legitimacy; knowing some of your details does not make a caller your bank.

text: Please don't visit the branch for this, the branch staff cannot update online KYC and they will make you come three times. I will finish it with you right now on the phone.
tell: Discouraging a branch visit keeps you away from the one place that would confirm the call is fake.

text: Do not disconnect or put the call on hold. If the session breaks, the verification restarts from zero and your account goes into freeze status automatically.
tell: Hanging up to call your bank back is the correct move, which is exactly what this threat discourages.

text: Don't share this process with anyone else in the family. The KYC link is tied to your personal biometric and becomes invalid if somebody else opens it.
tell: Technical-sounding reason for secrecy; a family member would recognise the scam.

text: Your account is already restricted and only incoming transactions are allowed. In thirty minutes outgoing payments will stop as well, and your salary will not be credited this month.
tell: Threatens income and daily payments on a short clock to push you past verification.

text: Today is the last date for KYC compliance. After midnight the account will be closed and your balance transferred to the RBI unclaimed deposit fund.
tell: Unclaimed-deposit transfer applies to accounts inactive for years, not to a missed phone KYC deadline.

text: Sir, I am saying this for your own benefit, please do it fast. There are two hundred customers waiting in my queue and after this call your ticket will be cancelled.
tell: Friendly-helper urgency: the caller frames speed as a favour so hesitation feels rude.

text: You will now receive a six digit code on your registered mobile for KYC verification. Please read it out to me so I can update your record in the system.
tell: That code authorises a transaction or account change; banks never ask you to read an OTP to anyone.

text: Download the app from the link I am sending, it is the official KYC support app. Once it is installed, allow it to view your screen so I can guide you step by step.
tell: A screen-sharing app gives the caller your OTPs and banking screens; official KYC never needs one.

text: Enter your debit card number and ATM PIN on the verification page to confirm you are the genuine account holder. The page is fully secured by the bank.
tell: No legitimate page asks for your ATM PIN; the 'verification page' is a phishing form.
